title: Eye-contour skincare: a 2026 narrative review of retinoids, peptides, antioxidants and depigmenting agents alongside procedures
headline: A company-authored narrative review concludes eye-contour products help hydration, firmness, pigment evenness and puffiness, but says the underlying studies are short, industry-sponsored, mostly of finished products rather than single ingredients, and low in diversity.
evidenceTier: Narrative review, abstract read; free full text not opened
fit: No new product or protocol; the authors' own limits statement is the useful part. Not specific to deeper skin tones.
displaces: Fits nowhere new; if an eye product is already used, nothing here argues for changing it.
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
summaryPoints: Abstract (read): PubMed search 2010 to 2025; retinoids, peptides, antioxidants, vasomodulators and depigmenting agents improve hydration, firmness, pigment uniformity and puffiness, 'particularly alongside aesthetic procedures'.

Authors' own limits: most evidence comes from finished multicomponent formulations rather than isolated ingredients; studies are short, industry-sponsored, and limited in participant diversity and endpoints.
Two of the authors are affiliated with ISDIN's innovation and development team (a skincare company). No searchable numbers in the abstract.
Follows the 25 Oct run's PDRN-versus-retinol eye cream entry: nothing here changes it.
toneData: Not reported in the abstract; authors note limited diversity
fitLine: Generic review; no deep-skin data or new product.
